readmeExcerpt:
# AG-UI: The Agent-User Interaction Protocol AG-UI is an open, lightweight, event-based protocol that standardizes how AI agents connect to user-facing applications. Built for simplicity and flexibility, it enables seamless integration between AI agents, real time user context, and user interfaces. ---

Join our Discord →     Read the Docs →     Go to the AG-UI Dojo →     Follow us → ## 🚀 Getting Started Create a new AG-UI application in seconds: ```bash npx create-ag-ui-app my-agent-app ```

Useful Links:

- [The AG-UI Dojo](https://dojo.ag-ui.com/) - [Build AG-UI-powered applications(Quickstart)](https://docs.ag-ui.com/quickstart/applications) - [Build new AG-UI framework integrations (Quickstart)](https://go.copilotkit.ai/agui-contribute) - [Book a call to discuss an AG-UI integration with a new framework](https://calendly.com/markus-copilotkit/ag-ui) - [Join the Discord Community](https://discord.gg/Jd3FzfdJa8) ## What is AG-UI? AG-UI is an open, lightweight, event-based protocol for agent-human interaction, designed for simplicity & flexibility: - During agent executions, agent backends **emit events _compatible_ with one of AG-UI's ~16 standard event types** - Agent backends can **accept one of a few simple AG-UI compatible inputs** as arguments **AG-UI includes a flexible middleware layer** that ensures compatibility across diverse environments: - Works with **any event transport** (SSE, WebSockets, webhooks, etc.) - Allows for **loose event format matching**, enabling broad agent and app interoperability It also ships with a **reference HTTP implementation** and **default connector** to help teams get started fast. [Learn more about the specs →](https://go.copilotkit.ai/ag-ui-introduction) ## Why AG-UI? AG-UI was developed based on real-world requirements and practical experience building in-app agent interactions. ## Where does AGUI fit in the agentic protocol stack? AG-UI is complementary to the other 2 top agentic protocols - MCP gives agents tools - A2A allows agents to communicate with other agents - AG-UI brings agents into user-facing applications
## 🚀 Features - 💬 Real-time agentic chat with streaming - 🔄 Bi-directional state synchronization - 🧩 Generative UI and structured messages - 🧠 Real-time context enrichment - 🛠️ Frontend tool integration - 🧑‍💻 Human-in-the-loop collaboration ## 🛠 Supported Integrations AG-UI was born from CopilotKit's initial **partnership** with LangChain and CrewAI - and brings the incredibly popular #### @ag-ui/langgraph@0.0.46

- Read LangGraph's native `Interrupt.response_schema` field (langgraph >= 1.2.12), falling back to value-level `responseSchema`/`response_schema` keys.
- Unwrap LangChain-serialized `ToolMessage` outputs under `kwargs` on tool end so tool calls and results emit correctly.
- Skip `on_tool_end` outputs with no tool call id instead of throwing or emitting events with an undefined id.
- Declare `protocolVersion` on `RUN_STARTED` events.
- Refreshed Gemini thinking demos.

##### Breaking changes

- `@ag-ui/client` and related peer dependencies now require >=1.0.0; `utils.ts` uses `contentToText`/`contentHasMedia`, which only exist in 1.0.

readmeHtml:
AG-UI: The Agent-User Interaction Protocol

AG-UI is an open, lightweight, event-based protocol that standardizes how AI agents connect to user-facing applications. Built for simplicity and flexibility, it enables seamless integration between AI agents, real time user context, and user interfaces.


Join our Discord →     Read the Docs →     Go to the AG-UI Dojo →     Follow us →

🚀 Getting Started

Create a new AG-UI application in seconds:

npx create-ag-ui-app my-agent-app

Useful Links:

  • The AG-UI Dojo
  • Build AG-UI-powered applications(Quickstart)
  • Build new AG-UI framework integrations (Quickstart)
  • Book a call to discuss an AG-UI integration with a new framework
  • Join the Discord Community

What is AG-UI?

AG-UI is an open, lightweight, event-based protocol for agent-human interaction, designed for simplicity & flexibility:

  • During agent executions, agent backends emit events compatible with one of AG-UI's ~16 standard event types
  • Agent backends can accept one of a few simple AG-UI compatible inputs as arguments

AG-UI includes a flexible middleware layer that ensures compatibility across diverse environments:

  • Works with any event transport (SSE, WebSockets, webhooks, etc.)
  • Allows for loose event format matching, enabling broad agent and app interoperability

It also ships with a reference HTTP implementation and default connector to help teams get started fast.

Learn more about the specs →

Why AG-UI?

AG-UI was developed based on real-world requirements and practical experience building in-app agent interactions.

Where does AGUI fit in the agentic protocol stack?

AG-UI is complementary to the other 2 top agentic protocols

  • MCP gives agents tools
  • A2A allows agents to communicate with other agents
  • AG-UI brings agents into user-facing applications

🚀 Features

  • 💬 Real-time agentic chat with streaming
  • 🔄 Bi-directional state synchronization
  • 🧩 Generative UI and structured messages
  • 🧠 Real-time context enrichment
  • 🛠️ Frontend tool integration
  • 🧑‍💻 Human-in-the-loop collaboration

🛠 Supported Integrations

AG-UI was born from CopilotKit's initial partnership with LangChain and CrewAI - and brings the incredibly popular agent-user-interactivity infrastructure to the wider agentic ecosystem.

1st party = the platforms that have AG‑UI built in and provide documentation for guidance.

aiSummary.oneLiner: Event‑based protocol that standardizes real‑time AI agent interaction with user interfaces
aiSummary.whatItDoes: AG-UI solves the lack of a common contract for streaming agent events to front‑end applications. It defines ~16 standard event types and a minimal set of inputs that agent backends can emit or accept. The protocol is transport‑agnostic, working over SSE, WebSockets, webhooks or any custom channel. A reference HTTP implementation and default connector let teams bootstrap an integration in minutes. Its middleware layer provides loose event format matching, enabling interoperability across diverse agent frameworks and UI stacks.
keyFeatures: Standard event schema: Defines about sixteen interoperable event types for agent‑to‑UI communication.
Transport agnostic: Works with SSE, WebSockets, webhooks or custom transports without code changes.
Bi‑directional state sync: Keeps UI state and agent context synchronized in real time.
Generative UI messages: Supports structured and UI‑rich payloads that can render dynamic components.
Middleware layer: Performs loose format matching and compatibility adaptation across frameworks.

useCases.title: In‑app AI assistants
useCases.description: Developers embed conversational agents directly into web or mobile apps, using AG‑UI to stream chat and UI updates without building custom protocols.

useCases.title: Customer support chatbots
useCases.description: Support teams deploy AI‑driven bots that exchange events with the support UI, enabling real‑time context enrichment and handoff to human agents.

useCases.title: Tool‑augmented IDE extensions
useCases.description: IDE plugins use AG‑UI to synchronize code suggestions, tool usage, and user actions, providing a seamless human‑in‑the‑loop experience.

useCases.title: Real‑time data dashboards with AI insights
useCases.description: Analytics dashboards integrate agents that push streaming insights and UI widgets, keeping visualizations in sync with live data.

useCases.title: Multi‑agent collaboration tools
useCases.description: Platforms that coordinate several agents leverage AG‑UI to share state and events across agents and the collaborative UI layer.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Frontend developers and AI engineers building interactive agent‑powered applications. Requires familiarity with TypeScript/JavaScript and event‑driven architectures. Ideal for teams that need a lightweight, cross‑framework contract for real‑time agent communication.
